title: Aurora Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Aurora Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered high-level timeline, confederation of hosted vs private deployment options, security/compliance requests (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), pilot metrics (latency/cost targets), and next steps to share docs and provision trial capacity.
topics: Deployment options: Hosted vs Private vs Dedicated
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Eric Chen (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Aurora - Head ML Ops), Tom Rivera (Aurora CTO), Priya Singh (Aurora Security), Sam Park (Aurora Data Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Diego and Eric. We wanted to kick off the onboarding and run through timeline, technical needs, and security asks. Can folks introduce quickly?
[00:08] Karen: Hi I'm Karen, I lead ML Ops at Aurora. We're excited to get this moving.
[00:12] Tom: Tom here, CTO. Main things for us: predictable latency, cost control, and no surprises on compliance.
[00:19] Priya: Priya, security. We'll need SOC2, ISO docs, KMS details, and some proof on audit logs.
[00:25] Sam: Sam, data engineering. I'll be running integration and helping with test dataset.
[00:30] Diego: Great, we usually run a 4-week pilot: week one provisioning and test prompts, week two baseline benchmarks, week three optimizations (batching/caching), week four UAT and handoff. Does that align?
[00:40] Tom: Sounds good, though timeline might slip if the private deployment is needed.
[00:45] Eric: A quick note: for private we provide a private control plane and customer-managed VPC, and an on-prem option for air-gapped setups. There are some additional steps for network setup and KMS integration that add a week or two depending on your security approvals.
[00:58] Priya: For KMS, we use AWS KMS, and we need to know whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys and whether keys ever leave our control. Also, what about HSM?
[01:05] Eric: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys. HSM integrations are available for enterprise private deployments; we'll share the integration guide.
[01:12] Karen: On the technical criteria, our SLO is 95th percentile latency under 450ms for short completions (<=128 tokens) and we'd like cost per 1k tokens under $X - we'll confirm the dollar target after the call. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[01:28] Maya: On hosted, our verified models usually meet similar latency targets depending on region and model choice; if not, Dedicated reserved pools can guarantee throughput and latency. Part of the pilot is model selection and benchmark runs - we'll run the same prompts you use in production to produce an apples-to-apples comparison.
[01:45] Tom: Ok, model selection: we have a mix of instruction-following and some domain-tuned models. We'll likely start with an open LLM and then consider a tuned variant.
[01:54] Eric: We recommend starting with a quantized variant for cost and then iterate. Also, prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching are low hanging fruit to control per-token cost.
[02:04] Sam: For integrations, we have a microservice in Kubernetes that calls the LLM. Ideally we can use a private endpoint inside our VPC. How do you do routing and fallbacks?
[02:13] Diego: Requests can be routed by policy - latency first for your critical endpoints, cost-first for async jobs. We also have automatic fallback to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained.
[02:22] Priya: On audit logs: we need logs that show request/response metadata, user ids, timestamps, and cryptographic proof of integrity for a rolling 12 months. Is that available in the private deployment?
[02:34] Eric: Yes, we capture per-request metadata and can integrate with your SIEM. For hosted customers we keep audit logs with configurable retention; with Private deployments you control the storage. We'll share a sample schema.
[02:45] Karen: Great. Also, SSO/SAML - we'll need SSO for the console and RBAC. Can we test a staging SAML connection?
[02:53] Maya: Absolutely, we'll coordinate Diego to help set up SAML in a staging environment.
[02:58] Tom: One more thing: data residency - some of our datasets must remain in the EU. Can Redwood pin regions?
[03:06] Maya: Yes, we can pin routing to regions for requests and hosts. For Private deployments you control region placement; for hosted we can route to EU cloud regions and confirm storage residency for logs.
[03:18] Priya: Ok that helps. On legal/contract side we may require specific language about data deletion and incident notifications. Who should we loop in?
[03:27] Maya: Diego will be the CSM point for operational requests and procurement touches. I'll loop in our legal liaison as needed.
[03:33] Diego: I'll follow up on contract language. I'll also attach our SOC2 package and the private deployment checklist.
[03:39] Sam: For the pilot, we'll want nightly batch jobs to run inference over 10k historical records to measure throughput and cost. Can you provision burst capacity?
[03:49] Eric: Yes, Dedicated pools support burst capacity. For a pilot we can provision a small dedicated pool for load testing. We'll estimate the GPU hours and provide cost guidance.
[03:59] Tom: About telemetry - we want token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the Console. Is there an API to pull that?
[04:06] Maya: Yes, the Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards and an API for cost exports. Diego will share sample queries.
[04:13] Karen: Good. Anything else on the technical front?
[04:16] Eric: One operational note: if you plan to use long-context calls, KV cache sizing matters; we'll want to know typical sequence lengths.
[04:24] Sam: Most calls are around 180 tokens avg, but we have some longer threads up to 800 tokens.
[04:30] Eric: Ok we might pick a model architecture that handles longer sequences or use windowing for the long threads.
[04:35] Maya: Let's align on success criteria - what should the pilot achieve for you?
[04:40] Tom: 1) meeting the latency SLO at 95th pctl, 2) cost per 1k tokens within our target, 3) security checklist satisfied (SOC2 docs, KMS, SAML), and 4) smooth integration with our K8s microservice.
[04:54] Karen: Also, a runbook for failover and fallbacks in production.
[04:58] Diego: We'll prepare a pilot runbook and sample prompts.
[05:02] Maya: Ok for immediate next steps, we'll send the onboarding guide, architecture diagram, SOC2 bundle, and a pilot estimate. We'll also schedule a separate security deep dive with Priya.
[05:12] Priya: Prefer that deep dive next week if possible.
[05:15] Diego: I'll propose a few times after the call.
[05:18] Maya: Any blockers we should know about?
[05:20] Tom: Our procurement usually takes 2-3 weeks; we'd like to start provisioning test capacity before final procurement if possible.
[05:26] Maya: We can start with a limited trial on hosted and then mirror to private if needed - Diego will propose the minimal agreement to kick things off.
[05:34] Karen: That works.
[05:36] Maya: Alright, recap and we'll send notes. Thanks everyone.

Meeting end.
